- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

input.approach_name: "Honest linear probing behind a hopscotch-shaped facade" — a single bin crate whose `tsl::HopscotchMap` is implemented as a power-of-two open-addressed table with linear probing, no tombstones (backward-shift erase), no neighborhood bitmaps, zero `unsafe`, and a bound-free cursor/iterator layer so the whole thing compiles in both edition 2015 (`rustc test15.rs`) and edition 2021 (`cargo build --release`).
module_layout: /output/Cargo.toml -> package manifest. Exactly one target: `[[bin]] name = "test15", path = "test15.rs"`. NO `[lib]` section, NO `src/main.rs`, NO `src/bin/`. `edition = "2021"`, empty `[dependencies]`, `[profile.release] opt-level = 3, codegen-units = 1, lto = "thin"` and DEFAULT `panic = "unwind"` (never `abort` — see risks). The existing /output/Cargo.toml already has this shape and needs no change.

/output/test15.rs -> crate root AND the ported `main`. The ONLY file that carries `#[path]` attributes: `#[path = "src/cxx/mod.rs"] mod cxx;` and `#[path = "src/tsl/mod.rs"] mod tsl;`. Contains the 1:1 translation of the C++ `main` (argv gate, stoi, insert loop, equal_range counting loop, `println!`). Holds no algorithmic logic beyond that so it stays auditable side-by-side with test15.cpp.

/output/src/tsl/mod.rs -> `tsl` namespace facade. `#![allow(dead_code)]` (the API surface intentionally exceeds what main uses), `pub mod hash; pub mod growth; pub mod table; pub mod hopscotch_map;` plus `pub use` re-exports of `HopscotchMap`, `Pos`, `Iter`, `EqualRange`, `Keys`, `Values`, `BuildMixingHasher`, `BuildIdentityHasher`. Because this file is named mod.rs it is a "mod-rs" file, so its child `mod` declarations resolve relative to /output/src/tsl/ with no further `#[path]` attributes (verified by compiling it standalone as a crate root).

/output/src/tsl/table.rs -> the bound-free storage layer. `pub type Slot<K, V> = Option<(K, V)>;` plus free generic functions over `&[Slot<K,V>]` / `&mut [Slot<K,V>]` that require NO trait bounds at all: `first_occupied`, `next_occupied`, `entry_at`, `entry_at_mut`, `occupied_count_debug`. Also the two probe primitives that take an ALREADY-COMPUTED home index so they need only `K: PartialEq` (`probe_find_from`, `probe_free_slot_from`) and the backward-shift compaction step parameterised by a `home_of: impl Fn(&K) -> usize` closure. Splitting these out is what keeps `Iter`/`EqualRange` free of `K: Hash + Eq` bounds (see risks — the existing hopscotch attempt in this tree fails to compile for exactly that reason).

/output/src/tsl/growth.rs -> the one place off-by-ones are allowed to live. `pub const MIN_BUCKETS: usize = 8;`, `pub const MAX_LOAD_NUM/DEN: usize = 3/4;`, `pub fn threshold(buckets: usize) -> usize` (= buckets - buckets/4), `pub fn grow_to(cur: usize) -> usize`, `pub fn buckets_for(n: usize) -> usize` (next power of two >= ceil(n*4/3), floored at MIN_BUCKETS), `pub fn mask(buckets: usize) -> usize`, `pub fn index_of(hash: u64, mask: usize) -> usize`. All total functions with unit tests; nothing else in the crate does capacity arithmetic.

/output/src/tsl/hash.rs -> `MixingHasher`/`BuildMixingHasher` (default `S`): a splitmix64-style finaliser with overridden `write_u32/write_i32/write_u64/write_usize` so integer keys cost ~3 ALU ops instead of a byte loop; `IdentityHasher`/`BuildIdentityHasher` mimicking libstdc++'s `std::hash<int>` (identity) for authenticity experiments; `pub fn mix64(x: u64) -> u64` used by both. All arithmetic uses `wrapping_mul`/`wrapping_add` (mandatory — see risks about overflow-checks).

/output/src/tsl/hopscotch_map.rs -> the public, C++-shaped facade. `pub struct HopscotchMap<K, V, S = BuildMixingHasher>`, `pub struct Pos(usize)` (the iterator/cursor stand-in), `Iter`, `Keys`, `Values`, `EqualRange`. Two strictly separated inherent impl blocks: an UNBOUNDED `impl<K, V, S>` (len, is_empty, bucket_count, end, advance, entry_at, iter, clear, into_iter) and a BOUNDED `impl<K: Hash + Eq, V, S: BuildHasher>` (find, get, insert_pair, insert, remove, equal_range, reserve, rehash). Contains the module-level doc comment that states plainly which hopscotch guarantees are NOT provided.
/output/src/cxx/mod.rs -> `cxx` shim namespace: `pub mod argv; pub mod runtime; pub mod string;` + `pub use string::{stoi, StoiError}`. Already present in the tree and already compiles clean.

/output/src/cxx/string.rs -> `std::stoi` reimplemented over bytes: `pub enum StoiError { InvalidArgument, OutOfRange }`, `pub fn stoi(s: &[u8]) -> Result<i32, StoiError>`, `pub fn stoi_with_pos(s: &[u8]) -> Result<(i32, usize), StoiError>`, `fn is_c_space(b: u8) -> bool`. Pure, panic-free, no I/O — so it is exhaustively unit-testable against the ~90 verified vectors.

/output/src/cxx/argv.rs -> `pub fn arg_bytes(i: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` (or a small `Argv` struct) built on `std::env::args_os()` + `OsStr::as_encoded_bytes()`; never `std::env::args()`, which panics on non-UTF-8 argv where the C++ binary succeeds. Also `pub fn argc() -> usize`. Models C++'s `argv[argc] == NULL` as `None` so main can raise the distinct logic_error.

/output/src/cxx/runtime.rs -> libstdc++ termination shims, each `-> !`: `pub fn terminate_invalid_argument_stoi()`, `pub fn terminate_out_of_range_stoi()`, `pub fn terminate_logic_error_null_string()`, built on one private `fn terminate(exception: &str, what: &str) -> !` that does `eprint!("terminate called after throwing an instance of '{exception}'\n  what():  {what}\n")` then `std::process::abort()`. Byte layout (two-space indent, TWO spaces after `what():`) lives in exactly one format string.

TESTS -> inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { use super::*; ... }` blocks at the bottom of table.rs, growth.rs, hopscotch_map.rs and string.rs. Deliberately NOT separate files and NOT /output/tests/: a `tests/` directory would be a cargo-only integration target that `rustc test15.rs` never sees, and a separate `tests.rs` module file would need its own `#[path]` juggling. Inline `#[cfg(test)]` costs the standalone build nothing (rustc compiles it out) and `cargo test` picks it up from the bin target for free.
input.core_data_structures:
DUAL-BUILD STRUCTURE (the binding constraint, solved first)

There is exactly ONE crate. A `[lib]` + `[[bin]]` split is impossible here: `rustc test15.rs` with no `--extern` flag cannot see a sibling library crate, so any `use test15::tsl::...` would fail standalone. Therefore all "library" code is plain `mod` files inside the single bin crate, reached from the crate root:

```rust
// /output/test15.rs   (crate root; also the [[bin]] path in Cargo.toml)
#[path = "src/cxx/mod.rs"] mod cxx;
#[path = "src/tsl/mod.rs"] mod tsl;
fn main() { /* ported C++ main */ }
```

Verified resolution rule: a `#[path]` on a `mod` item that is NOT inside an inline `mod { }` block is resolved relative to the DIRECTORY OF THE CONTAINING FILE — /output/ in both builds, because rustc resolves module paths against the source file, never against the process cwd. So `cargo build --release` (which compiles /output/test15.rs) and `rustc /output/test15.rs` from anywhere both find /output/src/tsl/mod.rs. Since the targets are named `mod.rs`, their own children (`pub mod table;` etc.) resolve inside /output/src/tsl/ with no further attributes. I confirmed the nested resolution by compiling /output/src/tsl/mod.rs and /output/src/cxx/mod.rs as standalone crate roots — every submodule file was located.

SECOND, EASILY MISSED HALF OF THE CONSTRAINT: `rustc test15.rs` with no flags compiles in EDITION 2015 (verified: `let async = 1;` is accepted by this toolchain's default invocation), while cargo compiles the identical bytes in edition 2021. The source must therefore be edition-agnostic. Verified-safe: `crate::a::b` absolute paths, `use std::…` in nested modules, `let … else`, `impl Trait`, `dyn`, `for x in [a, b, c]`. Verified-unsafe (compiles under 2021, HARD ERROR under 2015): `x.try_into()` and `Vec::from_iter(..)` / any bare `FromIterator`/`TryInto`/`TryFrom` use, because those traits are in the 2021 prelude only. Rule for the whole crate: import every trait explicitly (`use std::convert::TryFrom;`) or avoid them; also avoid explicit `.into_iter()` on arrays and avoid closures that rely on 2021 disjoint-field capture.

THE MAP

```rust
// tsl/table.rs — bound-free
pub type Slot<K, V> = Option<(K, V)>;

// tsl/hopscotch_map.rs
pub struct HopscotchMap<K, V, S = BuildMixingHasher> {
    slots: Vec<Slot<K, V>>, // len() is 0 (never inserted) or a power of two
    mask: usize,            // slots.len() - 1; meaningless while slots.is_empty()
    len: usize,             // live entries
    max_len: usize,         // growth::threshold(slots.len()); 0 while unallocated
    hasher: S,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub struct Pos(usize);          // the `iterator` stand-in: a bucket index
impl Pos { pub const END: Pos = Pos(usize::MAX); }
```

Why `Vec<Option<(K, V)>>` and not something cleverer:
- Zero `unsafe`. No `MaybeUninit`, no manual `Drop`, no drop-on-panic reasoning. `Vec`'s own drop glue frees the keys and values correctly, including on unwind.
- Exactly two slot states (Empty / Full). No tombstone state, because erase compacts (see algorithms). Every probe loop is a two-arm `match`, which is the entire auditability argument for this design.
- Memory parity with the C++ it replaces: `size_of::<Option<(i32,i32)>>() == 12` (4-byte tag + the 8-byte pair, align 4), the same 12 bytes/bucket as a hopscotch bucket holding `pair<int,int>` plus a 32-bit neighborhood bitmap. At count = 10,000,000 both need 16,777,216 buckets = 201 MB, with a ~302 MB transient during the last doubling. We are not trading memory for simplicity here.
- `Pos` is a plain index, which is the only honest Rust rendering of a C++ iterator: you cannot hold two live `&mut` cursors into one map, so mutation goes `map.entry_at_mut(pos)` rather than `*it`. That is a deliberate API shape change and it is why `equal_range_mut` returns `(Pos, Pos)` rather than a pair of mutable iterators.

THE ONE INVARIANT (everything else is a consequence)

  For every occupied slot j holding key k with home h = index_of(hash(k), mask),
  every slot in the cyclic interval [h, j) is also occupied.

Consequences relied on throughout: (a) a lookup may STOP at the first `None` — absence is proven by one empty slot; (b) probe loops always terminate, because `len <= max_len < slots.len()` guarantees at least one `None` exists (threshold is 3/4 of capacity, strictly less than capacity, and capacity >= 8); (c) insert preserves it for free by taking the first `None` at or after the home; (d) rehash re-establishes it by construction; (e) erase is the ONLY operation that can break it, hence backward-shift compaction.

EDGE STATE THAT MUST BE HANDLED FIRST, NOT LAST: the never-allocated map (`slots.is_empty()`, `mask == 0`, `max_len == 0`). This is what the `count <= 0` requirement actually exercises: `--a 0`, `--a -1`, `--a -2147483648` all construct the map, insert nothing, and then call `equal_range(&(count/2))`. Every bounded method starts with `if self.slots.is_empty() { return <empty answer>; }` BEFORE touching `mask` — otherwise `slots[hash & 0]` indexes an empty Vec and panics with exit 101 where C++ prints `0`.
algorithms: INDEX MATH (tsl/growth.rs). `MIN_BUCKETS = 8`. `mask(b) = b - 1` (b a power of two). `index_of(h, mask) = (h as usize) & mask` — low bits, one AND, no modulo, no branch. `threshold(b) = b - b / 4` (3/4 load; b=8 -> 6, b=16 -> 12). `grow_to(cur) = if cur == 0 { MIN_BUCKETS } else { cur * 2 }`. `buckets_for(n) = max(MIN_BUCKETS, next_power_of_two(n * 4 / 3 + 1))` for `reserve`. Mixing is the HASHER's job, not the index function's: `MixingHasher::finish` ends with a splitmix64 finaliser `let mut z = x ^ (x >> 30); z = z.wrapping_mul(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9); z ^= z >> 27; z = z.wrapping_mul(0x94d049bb133111eb); z ^ (z >> 31)`, so the low bits are fully avalanched and `& mask` is safe. Keeping the mixing in one place means `RandomState` (SipHash) can be dropped in via `with_hasher` and still index correctly. All multiplications are `wrapping_mul` — with plain `rustc test15.rs` (opt-level 0) `debug_assertions` and therefore `-C overflow-checks` are ON (verified via `rustc --print cfg`), so a plain `*` in the hasher would panic in the standalone build and wrap in the cargo release build.

LOOKUP: `find(&self, key: &K) -> Pos`. `if self.slots.is_empty() { return Pos::END; }` then `let mut i = index_of(self.hash(key), self.mask); loop { match &self.slots[i] { None => return Pos::END, Some((k, _)) if k == key => return Pos(i), Some(_) => i = (i + 1) & self.mask, } }`. Termination: guaranteed by invariant (b). No tombstone arm, no neighborhood window, no overflow list — this is the whole lookup. `get`, `contains_key`, `count` (returns 0 or 1) and `equal_range` are all one-liners over `find`.

INSERT (C++ `insert(pair)` semantics: DOES NOT overwrite). `pub fn insert_pair(&mut self, value: (K, V)) -> (Pos, bool)`. Step 1: `self.reserve_one()` — `if self.len + 1 > self.max_len { self.grow(); }`; this runs BEFORE probing so the probe indices stay valid. Step 2: probe in two phases to stay clear of borrowck: an immutable pass `fn probe_slot(&self, key: &K, mut i: usize) -> Result<usize, usize>` returning `Err(idx_of_existing)` on a key match and `Ok(idx_of_first_empty)` on the first `None`; then a single mutable write `self.slots[idx] = Some(value); self.len += 1;`. On `Err(existing)` return `(Pos(existing), false)` and DROP the passed-in value untouched — this is the semantic that guarantees unique keys and therefore `equal_range` length <= 1, and it is where a naive port that mimics `HashMap::insert` (overwrite) would silently diverge from C++. The two-phase shape also sidesteps the classic `match &mut self.slots[i] { None => self.slots[i] = ... }` conflict that forces people into NLL/polonius workarounds or `unsafe`.

GROWTH + REHASH. `fn grow(&mut self)` calls `self.rehash_to(growth::grow_to(self.slots.len()))`. `fn rehash_to(&mut self, buckets: usize)`: build `let mut fresh: Vec<Slot<K,V>> = Vec::with_capacity(buckets); fresh.resize_with(buckets, || None);` — NOT `vec![None; buckets]`, which requires `K: Clone + V: Clone` and will not compile for a general map. Then `let old = std::mem::replace(&mut self.slots, fresh); self.mask = buckets - 1; self.max_len = growth::threshold(buckets);` and reinsert with a specialised loop that SKIPS the equality check (all old keys are distinct by invariant): `for slot in old { if let Some((k, v)) = slot { let mut i = index_of(self.hash(&k), self.mask); while self.slots[i].is_some() { i = (i + 1) & self.mask; } self.slots[i] = Some((k, v)); } }`. `self.len` is unchanged. Hashes are recomputed rather than cached in the slot — that keeps the slot 12 bytes for `(i32,i32)` and costs ~3 ALU ops per moved entry with `MixingHasher`; for expensive keys (`String`) the natural extension is a `hash: u64` field in the slot, called out in the docs but deliberately not implemented. Amortised cost: the doubling series moves < 2n entries total. `reserve(n)` = `rehash_to(buckets_for(self.len + n))` when it would grow; `rehash(min_buckets)` mirrors the C++ member of the same name.

ERASE — THIS IS WHAT REPLACES NEIGHBORHOOD SHIFTING. Hopscotch's whole trick is that a displaced entry is moved BACK toward its home by swapping with an earlier entry whose own home permits it, keeping every entry inside a fixed-size neighborhood window and letting a bitmap answer lookups in one cache line. I implement none of that. The dual obligation — keeping the probe-run invariant intact after a removal — is instead met with Knuth 6.4R backward-shift deletion, which needs no bitmaps and no tombstones: `let mut i = found; self.slots[i] = None; self.len -= 1; let mut j = i; loop { j = (j + 1) & self.mask; let h = match &self.slots[j] { None => break, Some((k, _)) => index_of(self.hash(k), self.mask) }; let keep = if i <= j { i < h && h <= j } else { i < h || h <= j }; if keep { continue; } self.slots[i] = self.slots[j].take(); i = j; }`. The explicit two-branch cyclic test `h in (i, j]` is written exactly as in the textbook rather than as the branch-free `((h - i - 1) & mask) < ((j - i) & mask)` because auditability is the point of this design; a unit test asserts the two forms agree over an exhaustive small-table sweep. Consequence to document loudly: erase MOVES other entries, so it invalidates cursors to elements it did not remove — a fidelity loss versus hopscotch, where erase only clears one bucket and updates a bitmap. The ported program never erases, so this cannot affect its output.

CURSOR ADVANCE / ITERATION (all bound-free, in tsl/table.rs). `pub fn next_occupied<K, V>(slots: &[Slot<K,V>], after: usize) -> Pos { let mut i = after.wrapping_add(1); while i < slots.len() { if slots[i].is_some() { return Pos(i); } i += 1; } Pos::END }` and `first_occupied` = `next_occupied(slots, usize::MAX)` conceptually (implemented as a scan from 0). `HopscotchMap::advance(&self, p: Pos) -> Pos` returns `Pos::END` for `Pos::END` input plus a `debug_assert!(!p.is_end(), "++end()")` — C++ `++end()` is UB; we make it loud in debug and inert in release so a bug can never become an infinite loop. `Iter<'a, K, V> { slots: &'a [Slot<K,V>], next: usize }` and `EqualRange<'a, K, V> { slots: &'a [Slot<K,V>], cur: Pos, stop: Pos }` carry NO trait bounds and their `Iterator` impls call only these bound-free functions. This is the single most important structural decision after the dual-build wiring: the hopscotch attempt already sitting in /output/src/tsl/ fails to compile with six E0599s precisely because `Iter`/`EqualRange` call `end_pos`, `pos_after`, `entry_at`, `len` that were defined in an `impl<K: Hash + Eq, S: BuildHasher>` block.

EQUAL_RANGE. `pub fn equal_range(&self, key: &K) -> (Pos, Pos) { let f = self.find(key); if f.is_end() { (Pos::END, Pos::END) } else { (f, table::next_occupied(&self.slots, f.index())) } }`. Unique keys make this a 0-or-1 element half-open range, identical in LENGTH to the C++ result though not in which element `.1` names. `equal_range_iter(&self, key) -> EqualRange<'_, K, V>` wraps the same pair for idiomatic use; `equal_range_mut(&mut self, key) -> (Pos, Pos)` exists for API parity with the non-const C++ overload and hands back indices to be dereferenced through `entry_at_mut`. Cost: `find` is O(1) expected; the successor scan is expected O(bucket_count/len) and worst-case O(bucket_count) — the same linear bucket walk a C++ `operator++` does.

STOI (cxx/string.rs), byte-exact per the verified spec. `fn is_c_space(b: u8) -> bool { b == 0x20 || b == 0x09 || b == 0x0A || b == 0x0B || b == 0x0C || b == 0x0D }` — hand-rolled, because `u8::is_ascii_whitespace` omits 0x0B and `\x0b1` must parse as 1. Then: (1) skip `is_c_space`; (2) consume AT MOST ONE `b'+'`/`b'-'`, with no whitespace skip afterwards; (3) if the next byte is not `0x30..=0x39`, `return Err(InvalidArgument)` — this is the only source of that error; (4) accumulate `mag: i64` over the maximal digit run with `mag = mag.saturating_mul(10).saturating_add(d as i64)` (saturation, never wrapping — 5000 nines must not land back in range); (5) stop at the first non-digit and discard the entire remainder with no error; (6) `let v = if neg { -mag } else { mag };` — sign applied in the WIDE type, before the check, so `-2147483648` survives; (7) `if v < i32::MIN as i64 || v > i32::MAX as i64 { return Err(OutOfRange) } else { Ok(v as i32) }`. Base is hard-coded 10 with no prefix sniffing whatsoever (`0x1` -> 0, `08` -> 8, `010` -> 10). Operates on `&[u8]`, never `&str`, never `.trim()`, never `char::is_numeric`. `stoi_with_pos` additionally returns the consumed length; `stoi` delegates to it.

MAIN (test15.rs), a line-for-line mirror of the C++: `let mut count: i32 = 15; if let Some(a1) = cxx::argv::arg_bytes(1) { if a1 == b"--a" { match cxx::argv::arg_bytes(2) { None => cxx::runtime::terminate_logic_error_null_string(), Some(a2) => count = match cxx::stoi(&a2) { Ok(v) => v, Err(StoiError::InvalidArgument) => cxx::runtime::terminate_invalid_argument_stoi(), Err(StoiError::OutOfRange) => cxx::runtime::terminate_out_of_range_stoi(), } } } }` then `let mut map: tsl::HopscotchMap<i32, i32> = tsl::HopscotchMap::new(); for i in 0..count { map.insert_pair((i, i.wrapping_mul(12))); }` — `0..count` is empty for `count <= 0`, `wrapping_mul` because a plain `i * 12` panics at i >= 178_956_971 under the overflow-checks-on standalone build; nothing ever casts `count` to `usize` (i32::MIN as usize would be catastrophic). Then the faithful cursor loop: `let (first, last) = map.equal_range(&(count / 2)); let mut n = 0i32; let mut it = first; while it != last { n += 1; it = map.advance(it); } println!("{}", n);`. `count / 2` truncates toward zero in both languages, so it is left exactly as written. Nothing is ever written to stdout before the parse, so every abort path leaves stdout genuinely empty; `eprint!` is unbuffered so the terminate text reaches fd 2 before `abort()`.

SELF-CHECKS THAT COST NOTHING IN RELEASE. In main, `debug_assert_eq!(n as usize, map.count(&(count / 2)));` and `debug_assert_eq!(n as usize, map.equal_range_iter(&(count / 2)).count());` — three independent paths (cursor walk, presence test, iterator) must agree. Inside `rehash_to`, `debug_assert_eq!(self.len, occupied_count(&self.slots));` catches any resize that loses or duplicates a key, which is the failure mode the 4095/4096/4097 and 65535/65536/65537 evidence rows exist to detect. Inside the probe loops, `debug_assert!(probes <= self.slots.len())`. Unit-test matrix to write: growth.rs boundary table; table.rs backward-shift exhaustive sweep on a 16-slot table with a forced-collision hasher; hopscotch_map.rs insert-duplicate-does-not-overwrite, empty-map equal_range, single-element equal_range where the element is last in bucket order (so `.1 == END`), 0..N for N in {0,1,2,3,15,16,17,4095,4096,4097} asserting count==1 for the queried key; string.rs replaying all ~90 verified stoi vectors including the raw-byte ones.

input.perf_notes:
TARGET: C++ does 10,000,000 inserts + one equal_range in ~0.40 s (~40 ns/insert amortised, measured in the spec's evidence). Budget for this design: 0.3-0.8 s in `cargo build --release` / `rustc -O`. The dominant cost in both implementations is identical — one random access into a ~200 MB table per insert — so the achievable ratio is close to 1x, and the risk is entirely in constant factors.

SIZING. 12 bytes/bucket for `Option<(i32,i32)>`, power-of-two buckets, 3/4 load threshold. n = 10M -> 16,777,216 buckets (threshold 12.58M) -> 201 MB steady, ~302 MB transient while the last doubling holds old+new. Identical footprint to a hopscotch bucket array of `pair<int,int>` + 32-bit bitmap. Load right after a doubling is 0.375 and just before the next is 0.75.

PROBE COUNTS (linear probing, well-mixed hash). Unsuccessful search (= insert) costs ~(1 + 1/(1-a)^2)/2 probes: 1.8 at a=0.375, 8.5 at a=0.75, averaging ~3.7 across a doubling cycle. Successful search costs (1 + 1/(1-a))/2: 1.8 at a=0.6. Crucially those extra probes are CONSECUTIVE slots — 5 buckets per 64-byte line — so a probe run of 4 is typically still one cache miss. This is the reason plain linear probing is competitive with hopscotch here despite having no bitmap: hopscotch's bitmap buys a bounded window, not fewer cache lines.

REHASH. The doubling series moves <2n entries total, each a hash + a linear scan for the first empty slot with no key comparisons. Allocation is `Vec::with_capacity` + `resize_with(n, || None)`; the 201 MB fill is a ~20-40 ms memset-class cost, amortised.

HASHER. `MixingHasher` overrides `write_i32/write_u32/write_u64/write_usize` so an i32 key costs one xor-multiply-shift chain (~3-4 ns) instead of the default 4-byte `write` loop. Do NOT default to `RandomState`: SipHash-1-3 on a single i32 is roughly 10-20 ns including per-hash state setup, which alone could add ~0.15 s at 10M and would visibly widen the gap to C++. `RandomState` stays available through `with_hasher` for anyone who wants HashDoS resistance. `BuildIdentityHasher` (the exact `std::hash<int>` behaviour) is also available and is actually optimal for this workload — keys 0..n-1 land in distinct buckets with zero collisions — but it is not the default because it degenerates catastrophically for strided key sets.

BOUNDS CHECKS. Every probe indexes `self.slots[i]` with `i = ... & self.mask`; LLVM generally cannot prove `mask+1 == slots.len()` so a compare-and-branch survives. That is a predictable branch against an already-hot length field, ~1 cycle next to a ~80 ns cache miss. Keeping it (rather than reaching for `get_unchecked`) is a deliberate zero-unsafe trade; if a benchmark ever proves otherwise, the safe fix is to hoist `let slots = &self.slots[..]` and iterate a subslice, not to add `unsafe`.

BUILD FLAGS MATTER MORE THAN THE ALGORITHM. `cargo build` (dev, opt-level 0) will be roughly 10-20x slower and may take several seconds at 10M — always benchmark `cargo build --release`. The standalone path must be benchmarked as `rustc -O test15.rs`; bare `rustc test15.rs` is opt-level 0 AND has overflow checks on. `[profile.release]` should carry `opt-level = 3`, `codegen-units = 1`, `lto = "thin"`.

SMALL-INPUT COSTS. Default count = 15: one 8-bucket allocation, one growth to 16, ~15 inserts, a find and a short successor scan — microseconds; process startup dominates. `count <= 0`: zero allocations at all (the map never allocates), `equal_range` returns on the `slots.is_empty()` guard.

IF IT COMES IN SLOW, the escalation ladder in order of (benefit / added risk): (1) lower the load threshold to 1/2 — one constant in growth.rs, costs ~2x memory; (2) split the tag out into a parallel `Vec<u8>` control array so `(i32,i32)` pairs pack 8 per cache line — needs `MaybeUninit` and `unsafe`, so only under measurement; (3) cache 7 hash bits in that control byte to skip key comparisons — only helps expensive keys. None of these is needed for correctness and none should be done speculatively.
risks: FIDELITY GIVEN UP #1 — no bounded worst case. tsl::hopscotch_map guarantees a lookup touches at most NEIGHBORHOOD_SIZE buckets (a single bitmap test plus a short window), spilling to an overflow list when a neighborhood saturates. Linear probing has no such bound: with an adversarial or degenerate hash it degrades to O(n) per operation, and even with a good hash the tail latency at 0.75 load is a run of tens of slots. This is invisible to the ported program (sequential integer keys, mixing hasher) but it IS the headline property of hopscotch hashing, and this design does not have it. Say so in the module doc rather than letting a reader assume otherwise.

FIDELITY GIVEN UP #2 — different iteration order, so `equal_range(...).1` names a different element than the C++ does. Only the DISTANCE (1 if present, 0 if absent) is invariant, and only the distance is observable through this program's stdout. Any future ported test that prints `range.second->first`, compares iteration order, or depends on bucket layout would diverge. Unobservable here; unfixable in principle without reimplementing the real algorithm.

FIDELITY GIVEN UP #3 — erase moves other elements. Backward-shift deletion relocates entries to repair the probe-run invariant, so removing X invalidates a cursor to unrelated Y; hopscotch's erase clears one bucket and clears one bitmap bit, leaving other elements put. The ported program never erases, so this cannot affect output, but a port of any erase-plus-iterate test would break. The alternative (tombstones) preserves positions but adds a third slot state to every probe loop and needs a compaction policy — rejected as more total risk than it removes.

FIDELITY GIVEN UP #4 — none of hopscotch's tuning surface exists: no NeighborhoodSize/StoreHash template parameters, no overflow_size(), no min_load_factor / rehash-policy choice, no prime growth policy (power-of-two only). If sibling tests in this dataset touch those members, this map will need real additions rather than a rename.

COMPILE RISK, ALREADY REALISED IN THIS TREE — trait-bound stratification. I compiled the existing /output/src/tsl/ hopscotch attempt and it fails with six E0599s (`end_pos`, `pos_after`, `entry_at`, `len` "exist but trait bounds were not satisfied") because those methods sit in an `impl<K: Hash + Eq, S: BuildHasher>` block while `Iter`/`EqualRange` are generic over bare `K, V, S`. The mitigation is structural and must be designed in from line one: every cursor/iteration/storage primitive is a bound-free free function over `&[Slot<K,V>]` in table.rs, the unbounded inherent impl only forwards to those, and `K: Hash + Eq, S: BuildHasher` appears ONLY on the impl block containing operations that actually hash.

PANIC RISK #1 (the `count <= 0` requirement) — the never-allocated map. `mask` is 0 and `slots` is empty, so any `self.slots[hash & self.mask]` panics with index-out-of-bounds, exit 101, where C++ prints `0`. Mitigation: an `if self.slots.is_empty()` early return at the top of find/insert-probe/equal_range/remove, plus explicit unit tests for `equal_range` on a default-constructed map and for `count = i32::MIN`. Related: never write `count as usize` anywhere (i32::MIN as usize is 18446744071562067968).

PANIC RISK #2 — build-dependent integer overflow. Verified with `rustc --print cfg`: bare `rustc test15.rs` runs at opt-level 0, which turns `debug_assertions` (and hence `-C overflow-checks`) ON, while `cargo build --release` turns them off. So a literal `i * 12` panics with 'attempt to multiply with overflow' in the standalone build at i >= 178_956_971 but silently wraps like C++ in the cargo build. Every arithmetic op that can overflow — the `* 12`, the hasher multiplies, the mix64 chain — must use `wrapping_mul`/`wrapping_add` explicitly. Unit-test the wrap directly rather than relying on a 3-billion-key run to expose it.

EDITION RISK — bare `rustc test15.rs` compiles as EDITION 2015 (verified: this toolchain accepts `let async = 1;` from the default invocation), while cargo compiles the same bytes as 2021. Verified hard errors under 2015 that look perfectly fine under 2021: `x.try_into()` and `Vec::from_iter(..)` (TryInto/TryFrom/FromIterator are 2021-prelude-only). Also latent: explicit `.into_iter()` on arrays resolves to slice-of-refs in 2015, and 2021's disjoint closure captures can make a closure that borrows one field of `self` while another is mutably borrowed compile only under 2021. Mitigation: import every trait explicitly, avoid try_into/from_iter, avoid array `.into_iter()`, avoid clever closures — and add `rustc test15.rs -o /tmp/t15_2015` to the verification checklist alongside `cargo build --release`, because cargo alone will never catch this class of break.

STRUCTURAL RISK — the temptation to add a `[lib]`. A lib + bin split would make `rustc test15.rs` impossible (no `--extern` on that command line), and a stray `src/main.rs` or `src/bin/*.rs` would create a second auto-discovered bin target colliding with the explicit one. Keep exactly one `[[bin]]`, keep `src/` free of `main.rs`/`lib.rs`/`bin/`, and consider `autobins = false` as belt-and-braces. Note also that `rustc test15.rs` drops a binary named `test15` right next to `test15.rs`; always pass `-o /tmp/...` in scripts so the package root stays clean.

SILENT-CORRUPTION RISK — `Pos` is a bare index with no generation tag, so a cursor used after a rehash points at a DIFFERENT live element rather than dangling: a wrong answer instead of a crash. C++ iterators are equally invalidated but tend to fail loudly. Cheap mitigation if it matters: a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` generation counter on the map and on `Pos`, asserted on every dereference; it must not change `Pos`'s Copy/PartialEq behaviour in release.

CORRECTNESS RISK — backward-shift erase is the one genuinely subtle piece of code in the design, and the cyclic membership test `h in (i, j]` is easy to get off by one (the classic bug leaves an unreachable entry that `find` can never see again, which shows up only as a missing key much later). Mitigations: write the textbook two-branch form, cross-check it against the branch-free `((h - i - 1) & mask) < ((j - i) & mask)` form in a test, and run an exhaustive randomised insert/erase/lookup differential against `std::collections::HashMap` on a 16-bucket table with a deliberately collision-prone hasher.

COMPILE-TRAP — `vec![None; n]` requires `K: Clone + V: Clone` and will fail for a general map; use `Vec::with_capacity(n)` + `resize_with(n, || None)`. Similarly, the natural `match &mut self.slots[i] { None => { self.slots[i] = ... } ... }` insert loop trips borrowck; the two-phase immutable-probe-then-single-write formulation avoids it without `unsafe`.

DETERMINISTIC-HASHER RISK — `MixingHasher` is seedless, so a caller who controls keys can force collisions. Honest framing: the C++ being ported uses `std::hash<int>`, which is the identity function and therefore even more attackable, so this is not a regression; `with_hasher(RandomState::new())` is available for anyone who needs it.

ALLOCATION-FAILURE DIVERGENCE — at counts near INT_MAX the C++ dies with `std::bad_alloc` (or the OOM killer); Rust aborts with `memory allocation of N bytes failed` on stderr, also via SIGABRT/134. Same signal and same (empty) stdout, different stderr text. Out of scope for 'byte-identical stdout on valid inputs', but worth stating so nobody 'fixes' it later. Related: keep `panic = "unwind"` in the release profile — `panic = "abort"` would make an accidental Rust panic masquerade as the C++ abort (SIGABRT/134) instead of the loud, obviously-wrong exit 101.

PERF RISK — the estimates above are unmeasured. The two most likely misses are defaulting to `RandomState` (adds ~10-20 ns/insert) and benchmarking a dev build by accident. Mitigation: a scripted check that runs `--a 10000000` under both `cargo build --release` and `rustc -O` and compares wall time against /workspace/dataset/test15_executable directly, before any micro-optimisation is attempted.
